premise: The brilliant Indian mathematician who calculated the exact height of Mount Everest while working as a low-level computer in colonial India.
hook: He calculated the roof of the world using complex geometry, yet his name was initially entirely absent from history books.
key_facts: Joined the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India in 1831 as a 'computor'.
Invented new mathematical formulas for spherical trigonometry and surveying.
Calculated the height of Peak XV (later named Mount Everest) in 1852.
His exact calculation of 29,002 feet remained the accepted standard for decades.

premise: A college dropout who initially traded in ball-bearings builds a massive Indian supermarket retail empire from scratch.
hook: He started his career as a modest stock market speculator before building the country's most profitable retail chain.
key_facts: Dropped out of Mumbai University commerce studies after his father's death.
Initially traded in the stock market before launching the Avenue Supermarts retail chain.
Founded the D-Mart supermarket brand in 2002.
Became one of India's wealthiest self-made entrepreneurs.

premise: The bestselling novelist of all time whose mysterious 11-day disappearance triggered a massive national manhunt in Britain.
hook: The world's most famous mystery writer engineered a real-life disappearance that baffled police and captured global headlines.
key_facts: Disappeared from her home in Berkshire in December 1926 amidst personal turmoil.
Sparked a massive 1,000-police-officer manhunt involving airplanes and bloodhounds.
Found safe 11 days later registered under an assumed name at a Harrogate hotel.
Continued her career to become the best-selling fiction writer of all time.

premise: An orphaned daughter of emancipated slaves who built a haircare empire to become one of the first self-made female millionaires in America.
hook: Born into poverty just years after the end of American slavery, she turned a scalp ailment into a multi-million-dollar enterprise.
key_facts: Born Sarah Breedlove on a cotton plantation in Louisiana in 1867.
Suffered severe hair loss due to poor scalp health and harsh chemical products of the era.
Developed and marketed a specialized line of hair products and treatments for African American hair.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents, providing financial independence.

premise: The turning point when a fax machine salesperson used her entire life savings to patent and prototype shapewear.
hook: With only $5,000 in savings, she drafted her own patent using a textbook because she couldn't afford a lawyer.
key_facts: Worked as a door-to-door fax machine salesperson in Florida.
Cut the feet off her pantyhose to create a smooth look under white pants.
Spent her $5,000 life savings on the initial patent and prototype.
Founded Spanx without taking any outside venture capital.

premise: A self-taught mathematical genius from rural India who mailed his unproven theorems to British professors.
hook: He had no formal university training and failed his college exams because he spent all his time doing advanced mathematics.
key_facts: Grew up in Erode, Tamil Nadu, with access to only one outdated math textbook.
Failed his Fellow of Arts exam due to neglecting non-mathematical subjects.
Mailed a notebook of complex theorems to British mathematician G.H. Hardy in 1913.
Elected a Fellow of the Royal Society for his groundbreaking contributions to number theory.

premise: Shifting his Arctic expedition plans at the very last moment to chase the South Pole instead.
hook: He was sailing north to conquer the North Pole when he secretly changed his destination south, knowing his crew would mutiny if they knew.
key_facts: Initially planned an expedition to the North Pole using Fridtjof Nansen's ship, the Fram.
Learned that American explorers claimed to have already reached the North Pole.
Secretly redirected his ship toward Antarctica without informing the public or most of his crew.
Led the first expedition to successfully reach the geographic South Pole in 1911.

premise: A young American hitchhiker who traveled across Europe and the Middle East on foot to find spiritual truth in India.
hook: He left home with almost no money, traveling across continents with just a sleeping bag and a backpack.
key_facts: Grew up in Chicago in a middle-class family.
Hitchhiked across Europe and the Middle East during the early 1970s.
Crossed the border into India with minimal resources.
Became a prominent spiritual leader and author based in Mumbai.

premise: Risking a fledgling electronics company's future by deciding to target the American consumer market directly.
hook: He moved his family to New York City and rented a small apartment just to understand American buyers, despite having very little capital.
key_facts: Co-founded Tokyo Telecommunications Research Institute (later Sony) in post-war Japan.
Decided to abandon domestic branding conventions to sell products globally under the Sony name.
Relocated to Manhattan to directly oversee the American expansion.
Transformed Sony into a globally recognized consumer electronics giant.

premise: Spending years serving in the United States Air Force before getting his big break on television and film.
hook: Before playing iconic cinematic roles, he turned down a university drama scholarship to enlist as a radar technician.
key_facts: Served in the United States Air Force from 1955 to 1959 as an automatic tracking radar repairman.
Moved to Los Angeles in the 1960s to pursue acting while working as a transcript clerk.
Gained widespread recognition on the children's television show 'The Electric Company' in the 1970s.
Achieved major Hollywood film success later in his career.
